subject: Mandate binding / Decision Aspect
statement: Muse rejects the hypothesis that each governed Decision Aspect is evaluated under exactly one Mandate: unfalsifiable under analyst individuation, false under operational/independent individuation.
verbatim: Each governed Decision Aspect is evaluated under exactly one Mandate.
speaker: Muse
variants: docs/61-...:3588 — If the unit of analysis can be subdivided until the proposition becomes true, the proposition is not doing domain work.
notes: Hypothesis was the §31 surviving scope hypothesis; Muse also reverses its own earlier support for Decision-Aspect binding (3057-3059). Falsification is research evidence, not ratified ontology.

subject: Sizing as single-mandate decision
statement: Sizing is the strongest counterexample to single-mandate decomposition because size scales income, acquisition commitment, and tail exposure simultaneously; 'sizing → Preservation' judged arbitrary/category error.
verbatim: Size scales every consequence at once — income produced, acquisition commitment, tail exposure. There is no coherent single-mandate evaluation of “is this size right”; sizing is where mandates collide, not where they separate.
speaker: Muse
variants: docs/61-...:3234 — The prior example `sizing → Preservation` is explicitly rejected as a category error.
notes: Also CSP strike/premium substitution counterexample (3119-3135): strike→Acquisition, premium→Income decomposition loses joint trade-off.

subject: Declared mandate vs applied frame
statement: Muse distinguishes durable declared mandate/standing purpose (recorded, persists during inactivity, e.g., earmarked cash, dry powder, reserves) from a transient applied frame used during a specific decision; decision evaluation inherits from prior declared governance.
verbatim: Decision aspects do not create durable mandate binding. If anything, decision evaluation inherits from prior declared governance.
speaker: Muse
section: §32 Attack 2 — Mandates can exist when no decision exists
notes: Capital remains governed even when no transaction is contemplated — relevant to idle capital and Governed Quantity semantics.

subject: Telic Objective vs atelic Purpose
statement: Muse reclassifies Acquisition/Disposition as telic Objectives (completable desired state transitions) rather than Mandates; Income/Growth are atelic ongoing purposes; acquisition-through-assignment maps to Outcome Stance and disposition inventory to Inventory Role.
verbatim: Acquisition and Disposition are Objectives / desired state transitions, not Mandates.
speaker: Muse
variants: docs/61-...:3509-3518 — Muse terminology: Objective = telic/completable; Purpose = atelic/ongoing
proposed_destination: domain-model: Objective / Allocation Purpose / Outcome Stance
notes: Directly challenges §27 Principal Portfolio Mandate survey (Principal PASS for Acquisition/Disposition), §29, §30. Reconciliation warning (3472): parsimony argument, not clean counterexample falsification; needs independent challenge.

subject: Preservation as Constraint family
statement: Muse demotes Preservation from Mandate to a Constraint family (nominal-loss bounds, survivability, risk limits); applied to all capital it is non-discriminating; T-bill reserve specimen needs no Preservation Mandate.
verbatim: “Do not blow up” is a boundary, not a purpose.
speaker: Muse
variants: docs/61-...:3714-3732 — ChatGPT: Preservation receives especially strong reduction pressure; falsifier proposed
notes: Demotion explicitly not ratified (3884-3890, 4008-4010).

subject: Mandate as universal decision-time frame
statement: Across non-options programs (passive accumulation, rebalancing, trend following, dividend growth, tail-hedge budgets, T-bill ladders) the operative frame is Policy/Constraint compliance or joint Pareto trade-offs, not Mandate decomposition.
verbatim: Mandate is neither necessary nor sufficient as a universal decision-time frame.
speaker: Muse
notes: Specimens are generic investing, deliberately outside Wheelwright context.

subject: Exactly-one-Mandate premise
statement: Muse argues the exactly-one-Mandate premise was unsupported: holdings carry heterogeneous 'purposes' (collateral is a use, charitable transfer a terminal objective, compounding an ongoing purpose, dividends a recurring contribution).
speaker: Muse
notes: Multi-purpose capital remains unresolved (3577-3580).

subject: Three-level purpose hierarchy
statement: Muse proposes Allocation Purpose (capital pool purpose, stable, declared, recorded) / Program Edge Thesis / Decision Machinery (predicates, Preferences, Constraints, telic Objectives), placing Income at purpose, Acquisition/Disposition at Objective, Preservation at Constraint.
verbatim: Allocation purpose is the only level where the word “Mandate” currently earns its keep.
speaker: Muse
variants: docs/61-...:3486-3492 — Allocation Mandate: durable, recorded, capital-budget level, “what this pool is for”
proposed_destination: domain-model: Allocation Purpose / Program Edge Thesis
notes: Program Edge Thesis entity status unresolved; Kiro later: has not earned entity status (4144).

subject: Mandate–Policy causal relation
statement: Muse rejects Policy→Mandate and deterministic Mandate→Policy; proposes Mandate declaration and Policy Rules as siblings derived from higher-order Principal governance, and warns of circularity if Policy creates aspects that receive Mandates to explain Policy.
speaker: Muse
notes: Declaring Income/Acquisition does not uniquely determine delta band, sizing, tenor, or profit target.

subject: Temporal integrity / anti-hindsight
statement: Distinguishing legitimate reconsideration from hindsight rationalization (adverse-put specimen: 'this was an Income trade') requires durable timestamped entry intent, willing_to_own(strike) result, changed-evidence vs changed-preference, re-label test, and intent-revision policy.
verbatim: A pure transient decision-time binding model has no memory. If today's frames are simply re-derived, it cannot distinguish plan abandonment from plan execution.
speaker: Muse
variants: docs/61-...:3654 — The system must know what the operator committed to before discomfort arrived. (ChatGPT, restating Inner Game requirement)
docs/61-...:4051 — The system must preserve what was decided before the position became uncomfortable. (Kiro)
notes: High-confidence per Muse (3566). Strongly aligns with 'persist facts; derive trust'.

subject: Recommendation composition without Mandate
statement: Veto cases (premium inadequate or ownership unacceptable → WAIT/NO TRADE) are reproduced by predicates alone; marginal cases can use Preference; Mandate may do design/governance work but be explanatorily idle in routine evaluation.
verbatim: Therefore Mandate may do work at **design/governance time** but be explanatorily idle in routine decision evaluation.
speaker: Muse
notes: WAIT/NO TRADE posture vocabulary relevant to existing ACTIONABLE/EDGE/WAIT postures.

subject: Mandate scope competing models
statement: Muse table: One Mandate per Program and per Program Phase falsified; per Capital Pool survives weakly (vacuity risk); per Inventory Block circular; per Decision Aspect rejected; unrestricted multiple Mandates vacuous; durable capital purpose + decision criteria survives strongly; No-Mandate-in-loop strongest current model.
speaker: Muse
notes: Inventory Block 'may be individuated by mandate' — circularity warning echoed by Kiro spine audit (4127).

subject: Controlled Mandate-variation experiment
statement: Muse proposes the discriminating falsifier: hold Evidence, Alternative, predicates, Constraints, Preferences, Objectives, Program and execution assumptions constant; vary only declared Mandate (e.g., Income vs Acquisition on same CSP); ask if governed Recommendations legitimately differ.
verbatim: Do the governed Recommendations legitimately differ?
speaker: Muse
variants: docs/61-...:3785 — The critical discipline is that **nothing except declared Mandate may change**. (ChatGPT)
docs/61-...:3894 — Hold all decision machinery constant; vary only declared Mandate; determine whether Recommendation legitimately changes.
notes: ChatGPT extended to five domains (3777-3783). Experiment validity: changing any other machinery invalidates (3896).

subject: Muse confidence calibration
statement: Muse: high confidence that Program/Program-Phase binding fail, Decision-Aspect false/unfalsifiable, temporal integrity requires durable intent, Policy-as-frame cases exist; provisional on no-Mandate-in-loop and allocation-only Mandate; unresolved on allocation Mandate runtime effect, multi-purpose capital, and Program Edge Thesis identity.
speaker: Muse
notes: Multi-purpose capital representation never resolved within assigned range.

subject: Governance-time vs runtime-time split
statement: ChatGPT frames a two-layer model: governance/design time (declared purpose, program choice, Policy design, risk boundaries, recorded intent, amendment rules) vs runtime decision time (state/evidence, predicates, Constraints, Preferences, Objectives, Alternatives, consequences, Recommendation).
verbatim: This is not ratified architecture, but it is now a serious contender.
speaker: ChatGPT
variants: docs/61-...:4012-4045 — Kiro governance/runtime contender adds Decision Subject, WAIT/HOLD Alternatives, human Action/departure
docs/61-...:4617-4648 — Codex semantic consequence diagram adds Inventory Role, Outcome Stance, consequence semantics
proposed_destination: domain-model: Governance vs Runtime Decision layers
notes: Converges across ChatGPT, Kiro, Codex; doc states convergence does not authorize change (4462).

subject: Recorded Intent / Objective semantic split
statement: ChatGPT possible split: Allocation Purpose/Mandate = durable governance provenance; Recorded Intent/Objective = position/program-specific, effective-time scoped commitment; Policy = mechanical rule; Recommendation = Policy applied to current evidence.
speaker: ChatGPT
notes: Says this may be cleaner than letting operator choose a current 'frame' at decision time.

subject: Policy Rule mechanism typing
statement: Policy Rule is an umbrella across distinct mechanisms (qualification predicate, hard veto/Constraint, Preference/ordering, Objective/target, lifecycle transition, reconsideration/attention, amendment, provenance/record-keeping); Kiro: umbrella may remain but mechanism must be typed; no eight new entities proposed.
verbatim: Policy Rule can remain the governance umbrella, while its mechanism must be typed or otherwise semantically distinguishable.
speaker: Kiro
variants: docs/61-...:3734-3763 — ChatGPT §6 Policy Rule may itself be too coarse
notes: Rationale: a hard Constraint cannot become a ranking factor; reconsideration trigger cannot become action recommendation; amendment rule governs Policy not trade; Objective completes while purpose does not (4089-4094).

subject: DecisionAspect burden of proof
statement: ChatGPT shifts burden to any actor retaining DecisionAspect: provide Mandate-independent operational individuation rule, single-frame under adversarial specimens, and added explanatory power; until then it remains an unratified research concept.
verbatim: If the unit of analysis can be subdivided until the proposition becomes true, the proposition is not doing domain work.
speaker: ChatGPT
variants: docs/61-...:4143 — DecisionAspect — has not earned entity status. (Kiro)
notes: Meta-falsification criterion has general methodological value (subdivision-rescued claims are empty).

subject: Model A/B/C research fork
statement: Three alternatives: A Mandate participates directly in runtime evaluation; B Mandate is governance/design provenance, not runtime evaluator; C 'Mandate' vocabulary is over-broad (Allocation Purpose, Program Thesis, telic Objectives, Inventory Roles, Outcome Stances, Constraints, Preferences, Policy). After Kiro: A weakest but not eliminated; B/C strongly favored.
verbatim: The next work should falsify these alternatives rather than blend them prematurely.
speaker: ChatGPT
section: ChatGPT analysis §8; §33 Strongest remaining competing explanations
variants: docs/61-...:3975 — Model B/C is strongly favored over Model A (Kiro)
notes: Model A residual refuge later closed by Codex §35 as 'no demonstrated irreducible runtime semantics' — still not ratification.

subject: Runtime Mandate effect (five-specimen collision)
statement: Kiro ran five controlled specimens (CSP Income/Acquisition; covered call Income/Disposition; cash/T-bill Liquidity/Preservation; long equity Growth/Income; strategic holding+hedge Growth/Protection); changing only declared Mandate never legitimately changed Recommendation; manufactured divergences always smuggled another variable.
verbatim: Changing only declared Mandate produced no legitimate Recommendation change.
speaker: Kiro
variants: docs/61-...:4221-4223 — Codex controlled run: five specimens → no independent Recommendation effect from Mandate.
notes: Hidden variables found: willing-to-own predicate, premium floor, exit target, Outcome Stance, Inventory Role, liquidity/nominal-loss Constraint, hedge budget, Program selection, Policy, Objective, Preference.

subject: Candidate Mandate taxonomy audit
statement: Kiro audit: Income and Growth = atelic Allocation Purpose (upstream only); Acquisition = telic Objective + Outcome Stance; Disposition = telic Objective + call-away stance/Inventory Role; Protection/Hedging category unresolved; Speculation under-tested; Liquidity Reserve overlaps Constraint/pool role; Preservation = Constraint family (pending challenge).
speaker: Kiro
proposed_destination: domain-model: Allocation Purpose / Objective / Outcome Stance / Inventory Role
notes: Explicitly records that Principal §27 PASS (for Acquisition/Disposition as Mandates) is reopened, not overturned.

subject: Principal §27 PASS vs Muse/Kiro demotion
statement: Principal's §27 survey passed Acquisition/Disposition as Portfolio Mandates; Muse and Kiro lean toward demoting them to telic Objectives; no resolution recorded in the assigned range.
verbatim: Principal §27 PASS reopened; Muse/Kiro lean Objective
speaker: Kiro
notes: Principal-originated survey result vs actor reclassification pressure; Principal adjudication not in range.

subject: Kiro governance-time vs runtime model
statement: Kiro's smallest supported contender: governance/design time (Allocation Purpose, Program selection, Policy design, Objectives, Constraints, Preferences, standing intent, amendment rules, authority+effective time) establishes runtime (Reconciled State/Evidence, Decision Subject, Alternatives incl. WAIT/HOLD, predicates, Constraints, Objectives/Outcome Stance, Preferences, counterfactual consequences → Recommendation → human Action/deliberate departure/execution).
speaker: Kiro
notes: Allocation Purpose 'does not disappear; it performs upstream design/provenance work' (4045).

subject: Anti-hindsight via effective-time record
statement: Kiro locates anti-rationalization in durable effective-time facts (willing_to_own at entry, Objective/Outcome Stance in force, Policy version, evidence available, authority + effective time, amendment reason/authority, explicit operator departure) rather than a Mandate label.
verbatim: The durable protection against hindsight rewriting need not be a Mandate label. It can be the effective-time intent / policy / evidence record.
speaker: Kiro
notes: Distinguishes changed evidence, legitimate governance change, natural plan resolution, deliberate departure, retrospective rewriting (4066).

subject: Inner Game fit of governance/runtime model
statement: Kiro tested the model against the Inner Game goal: precommitment reduces objective drift; WAIT/HOLD/LET RESOLVE as first-class Alternatives and attention-without-action reduce activity bias; Recommendation is system output while Action is operator-owned with recorded departure.
verbatim: Wheelwright should do enough routine reasoning that the human spends judgment on authority, exceptions, and genuinely new evidence rather than reconstructing routine process under discomfort.
speaker: Kiro
variants: docs/61-...:4287 — §34 companion goal wording
notes: Kiro says it 'restated the core behavioral objective in substance' — paraphrase, not Principal verbatim.

subject: Recommendation vs Action authority boundary
statement: System determines what the governed process says; operator determines whether it happens; not autonomous trading; human authority retained over money, action, exceptions, governance amendment, legitimate override, consequential judgment.

statement: Primary behavioral falsifier: mechanical state was available (shares, open OTM call near expiry) but AI supplied an unstated objective; once the Principal supplied the actual objective (recover basis via premium, ultimately have shares called away) the governed interpretation changed materially.

subject: Natural resolution / no manufactured activity
statement: Do not manufacture activity to avoid a pre-accepted outcome; natural resolution is a first-class governed path.
verbatim: Do not manufacture activity merely to avoid a pre-accepted outcome.
speaker: unknown

subject: Journaling/provenance — no journaling theater
statement: Where the system already holds state, context, Alternatives, Recommendation, rationale, choice, execution, lifecycle and outcome, it should not force manual restatement; human journaling captures new/private judgment; contemporaneous temporal provenance must not be silently replaced by after-the-fact memory.

speaker: unknown

subject: Process change vs abandonment vs departure
statement: Preserve distinction among process-consistent continuation, legitimate reconsideration (evidence/economics/governance/lifecycle changed), governed amendment with authority and effective time, and operator departure; do not moralize; permit deliberate departure while recording it as departure.
verbatim: Do not moralize the categories.
speaker: unknown

subject: Inactivity semantics
statement: WAIT / HOLD / LET RESOLVE / NO TRADE may not be synonymous; natural resolution is affirmative; sufficient evidence that nothing clears governance can yield WAIT, but insufficient evidence is not automatically WAIT; idle capital is not automatically failed capital.

speaker: unknown

subject: Sell-side-bias guard

speaker: unknown

subject: Contrastive-testing discipline
statement: Avoid Cartesian explosion; sequence baseline → single-axis contrast → two-axis interaction → adversarial counterexample; a dimension that never changes Alternatives, admissibility, consequences, comparison, Recommendation, attention, explanation, or required evidence is semantically suspect.

speaker: unknown
